issues.description: Field 'totalOrders' type differs between the problem statement UML and the reference implementation. The UML in problem_statement.md declares SealSaloon::totalOrders as int (UML: -totalOrders: int), while the solution implementation declares private long totalOrders = 0; in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java. This mismatch can confuse students about which numeric type to use and what the getter signature should return.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended type explicit and consistent. Either update the UML and any textual references in problem_statement.md to indicate totalOrders: long, or change the reference implementation to use int for totalOrders and its getter. Prefer documenting the intended type in the problem description so students know which type to implement.

issues.description: The scope of the SealSaloon 'stock' attribute is inconsistently described in the problem statement and instantiated in the reference implementation. Early in the textual requirements problem_statement.md describes a 'final Stock stock' initialized in the constructor (which implies an instance-level final field), but a later note in the same document explicitly requires that 'stock' be static ('stock attribute: This is shared across all instances of the SealSaloon.'). The solution implementation declares the field as a static final Stock (private static final Stock stock = new Stock();). This inconsistency (instance final vs static final) may confuse students whether to implement stock as an instance field or a static class field.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the ambiguity in the problem statement: either (a) change the earlier phrasing that mentions 'final Stock stock' to 'static final Stock stock' so both the UML/text consistently indicate a class-level (static) field, or (b) if the intent is an instance field, remove or correct the later note requiring stock to be static. Ensure the UML, textual description, and any tests consistently indicate whether 'stock' must be static.
